description:
Outcome: A court can never have two active bookings for the same slot, including simultaneous requests, from README and the owner's explicit request for a separate double-booking ticket.
Scope: Database-enforced active-slot uniqueness; safe migration from existing unconditional uniqueness with no unprotected migration gap; atomic conflict handling and SQLite-supported write transaction foundation; reuse canceled slots while preserving cancellation history. Excludes: member quota policy, cancellation authorization/cutoff action and UI.
Acceptance: Sequential duplicates are denied; concurrent independent connections targeting the same court/instant yield exactly one active booking; different courts or slots remain bookable; direct persistence cannot bypass uniqueness; canceled rows do not reserve slots; failed writes roll back and canceled records survive migration.
Behaviour: Useful occupied-slot errors, bounded contention handling and safe retries/rollback without partial writes. Do not rely on ineffective SQLite select_for_update.
Verification: make test database-constraint/migration regression tests, real concurrent independent connections against a file-backed SQLite database, canceled-slot reuse fixtures. Prerequisites: Court slot validation and booking persistence. Assumptions: SQLite retained; cancellation ticket later provides the user action; tests may construct canceled rows directly.
title: Prevent double bookings
